tools.name: exec
tools.description: Call with no parameters (or only filters, e.g. read*) to list the saved helpers per language. Run inline code in an interpreter (python, node, bash, ...). Use it to compute, filter or combine data in one call; a plain command is lang bash with the command as code. Code calls the saved helpers of its own language as fn.<name>(...) (python, node, ts, ruby; found when the call is made, so a helper the program just wrote works) or by a bare command name (bash); the listing shows exactly what to type. fn.<name>(...) runs the helper's entry function: ts/node the default export, else the export named <name>, else its only function; python the function named <name>, else its only public function; ruby self.call, else self.<name>, else its only singleton method. Every export stays reachable as fn.<name>.<member>(...). Helpers may also import each other. Another language's helper is run as a subprocess from the directory in $JAD_FUNCTIONS_DIR. Pass data as input: the program reads it from stdin as JSON. Print the answer to stdout; for a short structured answer write to the file named by $JAD_RESULT to see it ahead of the raw output. It waits up to block_ms; if the program is still running you get an id and it keeps going: use the async tool to wait for, list, inspect or stop it.

lang.description: Interpreter name, e.g. python, node, bash. Defaults to bash.

code.description: Program source, run by the interpreter named by lang. A plain command is lang bash with the command as code.

filters.description: Only with no code: list the saved helpers whose name or description matches every filter, case-insensitive. A filter with * or ? is a wildcard pattern (read*, *file*); any other is a substring.

input.description: Any JSON value, written to the program's standard input as one line of JSON. Without input, stdin is empty.

cwd.description: Directory to run in, relative to the workspace root or absolute. Defaults to the workspace root.

block_ms.description: Most time to block for the result. If the program is still running an id is returned; collect it with the async tool.

read_only.description: Set true for a call that changes no file: searching, listing, printing files, git log, diff or status. Read-only calls of one response may run at the same time, and plan mode runs only these. Under a bwrap or seatbelt sandbox only the plan-mode writable paths (by default the temp folder) are writable for the call; without one, read_only is your promise not to change files, and a session may be set to ignore it: the call then runs in order and plan mode refuses it.
